title: Stream Bridge: SDK Interaction Patterns and Compact Protocol - PRD Notes
content:
Purpose
This doc captures an alternative PRD sketch: a "stream bridge" abstraction for the Hosted API that unifies incremental generation, tool-call handshakes, and compact typed frames for SDK clients. The goal is an ergonomic SDK surface that makes progressive and resumable UXs easy while keeping server-side runtime simple and cost-predictable.

Context and motivation
- We already have many PRD drafts exploring partial responses, typed frames, and tool call protocols. Feedback from SDK engineers and partners: too many competing primitives, hard to implement cross-language, brittle client reconnection handling.
- Teams want an adapter layer that maps the server's incremental output into small, constrained events the SDK can consume, persist, and rehydrate across disconnects.
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: define a compact, versioned frame format + SDK-side iterator/callback patterns + minimal server guarantees (idempotency, resume tokens, strict ordering within a session).

High-level goals
- Provide a minimal bridge protocol that:
  - Encodes both free-text tokens and structured tool-call frames in the same stream.
  - Supports resumable sessions with small resume tokens (<= 256 bytes).
  - Enables client-side replay, checkpointing, and offline tool fallback.
  - Keeps per-token server behaviour unchanged (no additional round trips per partial frame).

Non-goals
- This is not a replacement for the full typed streaming frame system in the long term — it's a practical, backwards-compatible layer for SDKs.
- Not tackling auth or multi-tenant routing here (delegated to existing infra).

User stories
- As a mobile app engineer, I want to show partial suggestions and let users trigger a tool (calendar lookup) mid-generation without restarting the session.
- As an SDK maintainer, I want a single, simple API that supports listen/callback and resume so I can implement it across JS, Python, and mobile.
- As a product manager, I want metrics that tell me how often tool-handshakes occur, how many resumptions happen, and typical resume token sizes.

Core concepts and primitives
- SessionId: server-assigned per request (short string).
- BridgeFrame (wire): a versioned tuple encoded as newline-delimited JSON-lite or compact binary (proto optional). Fields: frame_type, seq, payload, resume_hint. All fields are small strings or base64.
  - frame_type: one of ["tok", "tool-call", "tool-result", "meta", "end"].
  - seq: monotonic integer within the session.
  - payload: token text OR structured JSON for tools (stringified) OR opaque base64 for attachments.
  - resume_hint: optional small opaque token that lets the client resume at this exact frame boundary.
- Severity of guarantees: ordering within a single session by seq; gap detection allowed (clients should detect seq jumps and request replay).

Why newline-delimited JSON-lite?
- Easy to debug in logs, implementable without heavy proto stacks. For production binary we can offer an equivalent compact form.

Examples (conceptual)
- Text tokens: {"frame_type":"tok","seq":"42","payload":"and the result is ","resume_hint":"rU3..."}
- Tool call start: {"frame_type":"tool-call","seq":"43","payload":"{\"tool\":\"calendar.lookup\",\"args\":{\"date\":\"tomorrow\"}}","resume_hint":"rU4..."}
- Tool result: {"frame_type":"tool-result","seq":"44","payload":"{\"ok\":true,\"events\":[...]}","resume_hint":"rU5..."}

SDK surface sketches (JS + Python parity)
- Stream iterator model (async):
  - for await (const frame of client.streamRequest(params)) {
      switch(frame.type) {
        case 'tok': render.append(frame.payload); break;
        case 'tool-call': await sdkAdapters.onToolCall(frame); break;
        case 'tool-result': sdkAdapters.applyToolResult(frame.payload); break;
      }
    }
- Callback model (shortcut for mobile): register callbacks: onPartialText, onToolCall, onToolResult, onMeta, onEnd.
- Resume API: client.resumeRequest(sessionId, lastResumeHint) -> returns replay of frames starting after that hint.

Tool calling ergonomics
- Tool-call frames are declarative; the SDK surface receives them as structured payloads. The SDK adapter should:
  - Option A: synchronously call client.provideToolResult(sessionId, seq, result) which posts a compact tool-result back into the stream. This keeps the server in the loop and preserves ordering.
  - Option B: allow offline caching: SDK can persist a tool result and later supply via resume with a "tool-result-cached" meta-frame.
- Safety: tool frames include a tool-provenance header (short id, version) so we can detect incompatible tool contract responses.

Resumability and offline recovery
- Resume hints are emitted frequently (every N frames or on semantic boundaries).
- The client persists the lastResumeHint and seq. On reconnect it calls resumeRequest(sessionId, lastResumeHint). The server validates and serves frames from the next seq.
- For partial tool-calls where the client triggered a local tool while disconnected, SDKs can inject a special meta-frame when resuming: {"frame_type":"meta","seq":"-","payload":"local-tool-insert","resume_hint":"..."}. Server can validate and merge if seqs align or else return a conflict meta.

Observability / Telemetry (minimal set)
- Events emitted: stream_started, frame_received (type, seq), tool_call_received, tool_result_submitted (client or server), resume_attempt, resume_conflict, stream_ended, frame_gap_detected.
- Payload for telemetry entries should include sample of seqs, sessionId, model id, route, client SDK version, and latency to first tool-call. Resume token size bucket also recorded.

Performance and costs implications
- Protocol is intentionally compact; emitting resume hints every 8–16 frames balances resume reliability vs. frame overhead.
- No extra server-side compute beyond current streaming tokens; tool-call framing is just semantic envelope.
- Storage: servers will keep a short-term session buffer for resume windows (configurable TTL, default 5 minutes). Longer resume windows require state costs; defer to Dedicated/Private options for longer retention.

Backward compatibility and migration
- Servers can emit BridgeFrame v0 alongside existing partial streaming protocol. SDKs detect v0 frames by presence of "frame_type" key.
- Migration plan: opt-in for SDK beta for 6 weeks, collect telemetry, iterate on grammar of payload.

Security considerations
- Tool-call payloads may contain PII. Enforce workspace policy that tool-call arguments are redacted when persisted. Resume tokens must not contain secrets; treat them as opaque handles.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics
- Developer adoption: SDK beta clients implementing stream bridge in at least 3 teams (mobile, web, python) within 8 weeks.
- Stability: resume_conflict rate < 0.5% in beta.
- UX: mean time-to-tool-start < 250ms for in-band tool-call handling.
- Observability: telemetry events appear for 100% of sessions in beta.

Open questions and tradeoffs
- Binary vs JSON-lite framing: iterate with internal infra.
- How large should the server resume buffer be by default? (5 min, 10 min?)
- Should we standardize a small proto spec now or wait until v1?
- Conflict resolution policy when client injects local tool results that conflict with server-side tool results.

Next steps / immediate todo (owners)
- Product: finalize minimal frame grammar and publish spec (Maya) — 2 weeks.
- SDK: implement streaming iterator and resume API in JS (Rory), Py (Diego) prototypes — 3 weeks.
- Infra: expose short-term session buffer config and resume endpoint (SRE ticket: JIRA-1257) — 3 weeks.
- Legal/Security: review tool-call persistence policy (Priya) — 1 week.

Backlog (nice-to-have)
- Compact binary framing with signed resume tokens.
- Tool-call simulation harness for SDK-local testing.
- Integrated client-side UI components for progressive responses (web and mobile).

Notes to reviewers
- Focus review on API ergonomics: is resumeRequest API sufficient? Do we need implicit reconnection?
- Check the tool-call lifecycle: does requiring client.submitToolResult preserve ordering and safety across reconnects?
- Telemetry: propose we add a thin telemetry flag to stream params to avoid high-volume environments spamming logs.

Changelog
- 2025-01-20: initial sketch.
- 2025-02-07: added resume conflict semantics and sample SDK iterator code.

End of document.
